definition: A covalent bond made by head-on overlap of two orbitals, so the shared electron density lies on the line between the two nuclei; the first bond between any two atoms is a sigma bond.

A covalent bond made by sideways overlap of two parallel p orbitals, so the shared electron density lies in two regions, above and below the line between the nuclei; it forms only alongside a sigma bond.
The mixing of atomic orbitals on one atom to make a set of new, identical hybrid orbitals that point in the directions the atom's bonds and lone pairs take.
Mixing one s and three p orbitals into four sp³ orbitals, found on an atom with four electron domains: tetrahedral, with angles of about $109.5^{\circ}$.
Mixing one s and two p orbitals into three sp² orbitals, found on an atom with three electron domains: trigonal planar, $120^{\circ}$ apart, with one p orbital left over that can form a pi bond.
